signals.name: No Acceptable Use Policy
signals.description: Rules for acceptable use of information and assets are not identified, documented, and implemented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not defined what constitutes acceptable use of information systems, data, networks, and other organizational assets, or when such rules exist but are not effectively communicated and enforced.

metadata.detection_notes: Review acceptable use policy documentation, verify user acknowledgment records, assess monitoring for policy violations, check for personal use guidelines, evaluate bring-your-own-device policies.

signals.name: No Access Control Policy
signals.description: Rules for controlling physical and logical access to information are not established based on business requirements.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not defined access control policies based on business and security requirements, or lacks rules governing who can access what information, systems, and facilities under what circumstances.

metadata.detection_notes: Review access control policy documentation, assess whether policies define access rights based on roles and business needs, verify policies cover both physical and logical access, check for least privilege principles, evaluate policy approval and communication.

signals.name: No Access Rights Management
signals.description: Access rights are not provisioned, reviewed, modified, and removed in accordance with policy.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks processes for managing access rights throughout their lifecycle, including initial granting based on authorization, periodic reviews, modification upon role changes, and timely removal when no longer needed.

metadata.detection_notes: Review access provisioning procedures, assess access review schedules and completion, verify access removal upon termination or role change, check for excessive permissions, evaluate privileged access management, assess access certification processes.

signals.name: No Inventory of Information and Associated Assets
signals.canonical_name: No Inventory of Information and Associated Assets
signals.description: Organization lacks a maintained inventory of information assets and associated assets with identified owners.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization cannot identify all information assets, lacks documentation of asset ownership, or does not maintain an up-to-date inventory of hardware, software, data, and other information-related assets.

metadata.detection_notes: Request asset inventory documentation, verify asset ownership assignments, assess inventory update frequency, check for automated asset discovery tools, review asset classification and criticality ratings.

signals.name: No Asset Return Process
signals.description: No process exists for personnel to return organizational assets upon termination or change of employment.
signals.applicability: Applies when organizations lack formal procedures to ensure all organizational assets are returned when personnel leave, change roles, or when assets are no longer needed, including physical devices, access credentials, and intellectual property.

metadata.detection_notes: Review offboarding procedures, assess asset return checklists, verify tracking of issued assets, check for unreturned assets from former employees, evaluate asset return acknowledgment process.

signals.name: No Authentication Information Management
signals.description: Allocation and management of authentication information is not controlled through a formal process.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks formal processes for allocating, managing, and protecting authentication credentials including passwords, tokens, certificates, and biometric data, or when users can select weak credentials without enforcement.

metadata.detection_notes: Review password policies and enforcement, assess credential issuance procedures, verify secure credential storage and transmission, check for default or shared credentials, evaluate multi-factor authentication requirements, assess credential rotation practices.

signals.name: No Contact with Authorities
signals.description: Organization has not established and maintained contacts with relevant authorities for security incident reporting.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not identified and documented contacts with law enforcement, regulatory bodies, data protection authorities, or other relevant authorities for reporting security incidents or seeking guidance.

metadata.detection_notes: Review incident response plans for authority contact information, verify documentation of relationships with law enforcement and regulatory bodies, assess procedures for when to contact authorities, check records of authority communications.

signals.name: No Cloud Services Security Management
signals.description: Processes for secure acquisition, use, management, and exit from cloud services are not established.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization uses cloud services but lacks established processes for securely acquiring, managing, and exiting cloud services, including assessment of cloud provider security, configuration management, and data protection throughout the cloud service lifecycle.

metadata.detection_notes: Review cloud service adoption processes, verify cloud provider security assessments, check cloud service agreements for security terms, assess cloud configuration management practices, examine data migration and exit strategies, review cloud access controls and monitoring.

signals.name: No Compliance Review with Security Policies
signals.canonical_name: No Compliance Review with Security Policies
signals.description: Compliance with security policies and standards is not regularly reviewed.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not regularly review compliance with its information security policies, topic-specific policies, rules, and standards, or fails to take corrective action when non-compliance is identified.

metadata.detection_notes: Review compliance monitoring procedures, verify policy compliance assessment schedules, check for compliance metrics and reporting, assess non-compliance issue tracking and resolution, examine management review of compliance status.

signals.name: No Information Security During Disruption
signals.description: Plans for maintaining security at appropriate levels during disruption are not established.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks plans to maintain information security controls and protections during business disruptions, emergencies, or crisis situations, including natural disasters, pandemics, system failures, or other adverse events.

metadata.detection_notes: Review business continuity plans for security controls, verify security considerations in disaster recovery procedures, check emergency response plans for security requirements, assess alternative operating procedures for security maintenance, examine testing of security during disruption scenarios.

signals.name: No Documented Operating Procedures
signals.description: Operating procedures for information processing facilities are not documented and available.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have documented operating procedures for information processing facilities, or when procedures are not made available to personnel who need them, potentially leading to inconsistent operations and increased security risks.

metadata.detection_notes: Review operations documentation repositories, verify existence of documented procedures for critical systems, check procedure accessibility and version control, assess procedure completeness and accuracy, examine procedure review and update processes.

signals.name: No Segregation of Duties
signals.description: Conflicting duties and areas of responsibility are not segregated to reduce opportunities for unauthorized modification or misuse.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization allows individuals to perform conflicting duties such as development and production deployment, financial approval and payment execution, or security configuration and security auditing without compensating controls.

metadata.detection_notes: Analyze role assignments for conflicting duties, review access control matrices for separation violations, assess financial and technical approval workflows, verify compensating controls where segregation is not feasible.

signals.name: No Information Security Event Assessment
signals.description: Security events are not assessed to determine if they should be categorized as incidents.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks procedures and criteria for evaluating information security events to determine their significance, impact, and whether they constitute security incidents requiring formal incident response procedures.

metadata.detection_notes: Review event monitoring and triage procedures, verify existence of incident classification criteria, check for event assessment workflows, assess decision-making authority for incident declaration, examine event logging and analysis capabilities.

signals.name: No Evidence Collection Procedures
signals.description: Procedures for identification, collection, and preservation of evidence are not established.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks documented procedures for identifying, collecting, acquiring, and preserving evidence related to information security incidents in a manner that maintains evidentiary integrity for potential legal, regulatory, or disciplinary proceedings.

metadata.detection_notes: Review evidence handling procedures, verify chain of custody documentation, check for forensic capabilities and tools, assess evidence preservation methods, examine legal admissibility requirements compliance, verify personnel training in evidence collection.

signals.name: No ICT Readiness for Business Continuity
signals.canonical_name: No ICT Readiness for Business Continuity
signals.description: ICT continuity requirements are not planned, implemented, maintained, and tested.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not planned, implemented, maintained, and tested ICT continuity capabilities based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements, including redundancy, backup systems, and recovery procedures for information and communication technology.

metadata.detection_notes: Review ICT continuity planning documentation, verify backup and redundancy implementations, check disaster recovery testing records, assess recovery time and recovery point objectives, examine ICT dependency analysis, verify business continuity integration.

signals.name: No Identity Management Lifecycle
signals.description: Full lifecycle management of identities is not implemented from creation through revocation.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks formal processes for managing the complete lifecycle of user identities including provisioning, modification, review, and deprovisioning across all systems and applications.

metadata.detection_notes: Review identity provisioning processes, assess deprovisioning procedures for leavers, verify identity management system capabilities, check for orphaned accounts, evaluate identity lifecycle automation, assess identity governance reviews.

signals.name: No Learning from Information Security Incidents
signals.canonical_name: No Learning from Information Security Incidents
signals.description: Knowledge from security incidents is not used to strengthen controls and reduce future incidents.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization fails to analyze lessons learned from information security incidents, does not implement corrective actions based on incident findings, or does not use incident knowledge to improve security controls and prevent recurrence.

metadata.detection_notes: Review post-incident review procedures, verify existence of lessons learned documentation, check for implementation of corrective actions, assess incident trend analysis processes, examine security control improvement initiatives based on incidents.

signals.name: No Information Security Incident Management Planning
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security Incident Management Planning
signals.description: Organization lacks plans and preparation for managing information security incidents.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have documented incident management plans, defined roles and responsibilities, established procedures for incident detection and response, or adequate preparation including training and resources for handling information security incidents.

metadata.detection_notes: Review incident response plans and procedures, verify incident management team structure and roles, check for incident response training and exercises, assess availability of incident response tools and resources, examine incident classification and escalation procedures.

signals.name: No Information Security Incident Response
signals.description: Security incidents are not responded to according to documented procedures.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have documented incident response procedures or fails to follow established procedures when responding to information security incidents, including detection, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident activities.

metadata.detection_notes: Review incident response procedures documentation, verify incident handling records and timelines, check for evidence of containment and recovery actions, assess communication procedures during incidents, examine root cause analysis and remediation tracking.

signals.name: No Independent Review of Information Security
signals.canonical_name: No Independent Review of Information Security
signals.description: Organization's approach to managing security is not reviewed independently at planned intervals.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not conduct independent reviews of its information security management approach, implementation of policies and procedures, and compliance with security requirements at planned intervals or when significant changes occur.

metadata.detection_notes: Review internal audit schedules and reports, verify independence of reviewers, check for third-party security assessments, assess review findings and remediation tracking, examine review scope and frequency, verify management review of findings.

signals.name: No Information Classification Scheme
signals.description: Information is not classified according to confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not established a classification scheme for information based on legal requirements, criticality, sensitivity, and value, or when information is not systematically classified according to such a scheme.

metadata.detection_notes: Review classification policies and schemes, assess whether information assets have assigned classifications, verify classification criteria align with business and legal requirements, check for classification guidance and training.

signals.name: No Information Labelling Procedures
signals.description: Procedures for labelling information according to the classification scheme are not implemented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has a classification scheme but lacks procedures for labelling information assets, or when information is classified but labels are not consistently applied to documents, files, emails, and other information containers.

metadata.detection_notes: Review labelling procedures, assess whether documents and emails include classification labels, verify metadata tagging in information systems, check for automated labelling tools, evaluate user compliance with labelling requirements.

signals.name: No Contact with Special Interest Groups
signals.canonical_name: No Contact with Special Interest Groups
signals.description: Organization has not established contacts with security forums and professional associations for threat intelligence.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization is not engaged with security communities, industry groups, information sharing forums, or professional associations that could provide threat intelligence and security best practices.

metadata.detection_notes: Review memberships in security organizations, assess participation in information sharing forums, verify subscriptions to threat intelligence feeds, check attendance at security conferences, evaluate engagement with industry-specific security groups.

signals.name: No Intellectual Property Rights Protection
signals.description: Procedures to protect intellectual property rights are not implemented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks appropriate procedures to protect intellectual property rights related to information assets, including software licensing compliance, protection of proprietary information, and respecting third-party intellectual property rights.

metadata.detection_notes: Review intellectual property policies and procedures, verify software license management processes, check for proprietary information protection measures, assess copyright and patent compliance, examine vendor license audits and compliance records.

signals.name: No Identification of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
signals.canonical_name: No Identification of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
signals.description: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to security are not identified and documented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not identified, documented, and maintained awareness of applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements related to information security and the protection of information assets.

metadata.detection_notes: Review compliance register or requirements documentation, verify legal and regulatory monitoring processes, check for contractual obligation tracking, assess requirements communication to relevant personnel, examine compliance assessment and gap analysis processes.

signals.name: No Management Security Responsibilities
signals.description: Management does not require personnel to apply information security in accordance with established policies and procedures.
signals.applicability: Applies when management does not actively enforce security policies, lacks accountability mechanisms for security compliance, or fails to demonstrate leadership in information security practices.

metadata.detection_notes: Review management communications regarding security expectations, assess security enforcement mechanisms, interview personnel about management support for security, evaluate consequences for security policy violations, verify management participation in security reviews.

signals.name: No Privacy and Protection of PII
signals.canonical_name: No Privacy and Protection of PII
signals.description: Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information is not ensured as required.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not identify and meet privacy and PII protection requirements applicable to the organization, including compliance with privacy laws, data subject rights, consent management, and cross-border data transfer controls.

metadata.detection_notes: Review privacy policies and procedures, verify PII inventory and data mapping, check consent management processes, assess data subject rights procedures, examine data protection impact assessments, verify cross-border transfer mechanisms, review privacy training and awareness.

signals.name: No Information Security in Project Management
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security in Project Management
signals.description: Information security is not integrated into project management regardless of project type.
signals.applicability: Applies when organizations run projects without incorporating security requirements, security reviews, or security acceptance criteria in project planning, execution, and delivery phases.

metadata.detection_notes: Review project templates and methodologies for security integration, assess project charters for security requirements, verify security checkpoints in project gates, check for security acceptance criteria in project deliverables.

signals.name: No Protection of Records
signals.description: Records are not protected from loss, destruction, falsification, and unauthorized access.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not adequately protect important records from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access, and unauthorized release in accordance with legal, regulatory, contractual, and business requirements.

metadata.detection_notes: Review records management policies and procedures, verify records classification and retention schedules, check access controls for records systems, assess backup and recovery for records, examine disposal procedures for records, verify compliance with retention requirements.

signals.name: No Information Security Policies
signals.description: Organization lacks documented information security policies approved by management, published, and communicated to relevant parties.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have formally documented, management-approved information security policies that are published and communicated to personnel and relevant external parties.

metadata.detection_notes: Review documentation repositories for security policy documents, verify management approval signatures, check communication records to personnel, assess policy review and update processes.

signals.name: No Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security Roles and Responsibilities
signals.description: Information security roles and responsibilities are not defined and allocated according to organizational needs.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has not formally defined and documented security roles, responsibilities are not clearly allocated, or personnel are unclear about their information security obligations.

metadata.detection_notes: Review organizational charts and role descriptions for security responsibilities, interview personnel about their security obligations, assess RACI matrices for security functions, verify documentation of security role assignments.

signals.name: No Information Security in Supplier Agreements
signals.canonical_name: No Information Security in Supplier Agreements
signals.description: Supplier agreements do not establish relevant information security requirements based on supply relationship type.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization has supplier agreements that lack adequate information security requirements, terms, and conditions appropriate to the type of supplier relationship and the information assets that may be accessed, processed, stored, communicated, or provided.

metadata.detection_notes: Review supplier contracts and agreements for information security clauses, verify security requirements are defined based on supplier access levels, check for security obligations and SLA definitions, assess incident response and breach notification terms.

signals.name: No Supplier Service Monitoring and Review
signals.canonical_name: No Supplier Service Monitoring and Review
signals.description: Supplier service delivery is not regularly monitored, reviewed, and audited for security compliance.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization does not have established processes to regularly monitor, review, and audit supplier service levels and information security practices to ensure ongoing compliance with security requirements and contractual obligations.

metadata.detection_notes: Review supplier performance monitoring procedures, verify existence of regular security reviews, check audit schedules and findings, assess change management processes for supplier services, examine incident tracking and resolution with suppliers.

signals.name: No Supplier Security Management
signals.description: Processes for managing security risks associated with supplier access to organizational assets are not defined.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks processes to identify, assess, and mitigate security risks in supplier relationships, including vendor due diligence, security requirements in contracts, and ongoing monitoring of supplier security posture.

metadata.detection_notes: Review supplier security assessment processes, verify security requirements in contracts and SLAs, assess supplier risk classifications, check for vendor security questionnaires, evaluate ongoing supplier monitoring, verify incident notification requirements.

signals.name: No ICT Supply Chain Security Management
signals.canonical_name: No ICT Supply Chain Security Management
signals.description: Processes for managing ICT supply chain security risks are not defined and implemented.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks defined processes and controls to manage information security risks associated with ICT products and services throughout the supply chain lifecycle, including supplier selection, onboarding, and ongoing management.

metadata.detection_notes: Assess whether supply chain security policies exist, verify supplier security assessment procedures, check for ICT product and service security evaluation processes, review supplier risk management documentation, examine controls for supply chain transparency and integrity.

signals.name: No Threat Intelligence Program
signals.description: Organization does not collect and analyze threat intelligence to inform security decisions and controls.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks a systematic approach to gathering, analyzing, and applying threat intelligence from internal and external sources to inform risk assessments and security control decisions.

metadata.detection_notes: Review threat intelligence sources and subscriptions, assess threat analysis processes, verify integration of threat intelligence into risk assessments, check for threat hunting activities, evaluate security control adjustments based on threat landscape changes.

signals.name: No Information Transfer Controls
signals.description: Rules, procedures, and agreements for secure information transfer are not in place.
signals.applicability: Applies when an organization lacks controls for transferring information between the organization and external parties, including procedures for electronic transmission, physical transport, and verbal communication of sensitive information.

metadata.detection_notes: Review information transfer policies and procedures, assess encryption requirements for data in transit, verify secure file transfer mechanisms, check agreements with external parties for security requirements, evaluate controls for physical media transport.

signals.name: No Security Violation Disciplinary Process
signals.description: No formal disciplinary process exists for personnel who commit information security policy violations.
signals.applicability: HR policies, security violation handling, policy enforcement

metadata.detection_notes: Review HR policies, disciplinary procedures, and incident response documentation for defined processes addressing information security policy violations.

signals.name: No Security Terms in Employment Contracts
signals.canonical_name: No Security Terms in Employment Contracts
signals.description: Employment contracts do not state personnel and organization responsibilities for information security.
signals.applicability: Employment contracts, contractor agreements, security acknowledgments

metadata.detection_notes: Review employment contract templates, contractor agreements, and onboarding documentation for inclusion of information security responsibilities and obligations.

signals.name: No Security Event Reporting Mechanism
signals.description: Mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected security events is not provided.
signals.applicability: Incident reporting channels, security awareness, reporting procedures

metadata.detection_notes: Review incident reporting procedures, available reporting channels, and personnel awareness of how to report security events. Verify accessibility and effectiveness of reporting mechanisms.

signals.name: No Confidentiality Agreements
signals.description: Confidentiality or NDA requirements are not identified, documented, and regularly reviewed.
signals.applicability: Employment, third parties, sensitive information access

metadata.detection_notes: Review employment contracts, third-party agreements, and vendor contracts for presence of confidentiality clauses and NDAs. Verify regular review processes exist.

signals.name: No Remote Working Security Controls
signals.description: Security measures for remote working are not implemented to protect information accessed or processed.
signals.applicability: Remote work policies, home office security, mobile device use

metadata.detection_notes: Review remote work policies, endpoint security configurations, VPN usage, and home office security requirements to identify gaps in remote working protections.

signals.name: No Personnel Screening
signals.description: Background verification checks on candidates are not carried out prior to joining and on an ongoing basis.
signals.applicability: HR processes, contractor onboarding, privileged access roles

metadata.detection_notes: Review HR onboarding procedures, background check policies, and verification records for candidates and existing personnel with privileged access.

signals.name: No Security Awareness Training
signals.description: Personnel do not receive appropriate security awareness education, training, and updates.
signals.applicability: All personnel, contractors, regular training programs

metadata.detection_notes: Review training records, security awareness program documentation, and onboarding materials to verify presence and currency of security education initiatives.

signals.name: No Post-Employment Security Process
signals.description: Security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change are not defined and enforced.
signals.applicability: Offboarding, role changes, confidentiality obligations

metadata.detection_notes: Review offboarding procedures, access revocation processes, and post-employment obligation documentation to verify comprehensive security controls during employment transitions.

signals.name: No Cabling Security
signals.description: Cables carrying power and data are not protected from interception, interference, or damage.
signals.applicability: Organizations with power and data cabling infrastructure requiring protection from unauthorized access, tampering, and physical damage

metadata.detection_notes: Assess cabling infrastructure for protection against interception (shielding, encryption), interference (separation from power), and damage (conduit, labeling, access control). Exposed cables, poor cable management, or unprotected cable runs indicate this deficiency.

signals.name: No Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy
signals.canonical_name: No Clear Desk and Clear Screen Policy
signals.description: Clear desk and clear screen rules for papers and removable storage media are not defined and enforced.
signals.applicability: Organizations where personnel handle sensitive information in physical form or on computer screens that could be viewed by unauthorized persons

metadata.detection_notes: Review policies for clear desk (securing physical documents when unattended) and clear screen (locking workstations when away). Absence of documented policies, lack of enforcement, or observation of unattended sensitive materials indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Physical Entry Controls
signals.description: Secure areas are not protected by appropriate entry controls and access points.
signals.applicability: Organizations with secure areas requiring controlled access to protect sensitive information and assets

metadata.detection_notes: Examine access control mechanisms at entry points to secure areas. Look for absence of badge readers, locks, security personnel, visitor management systems, or access logs. Unrestricted entry to sensitive areas indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Equipment Maintenance Controls
signals.description: Equipment is not maintained correctly to ensure availability and integrity.
signals.applicability: Organizations with information processing equipment requiring regular maintenance to ensure continued operation and data integrity

metadata.detection_notes: Review equipment maintenance schedules, service records, vendor qualifications, and data protection during maintenance. Absence of maintenance schedules, unqualified service providers, or lack of data protection procedures indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Equipment Siting and Protection
signals.description: Equipment is not sited securely and protected against environmental threats and unauthorized access.
signals.applicability: Organizations with information processing equipment that requires protection from environmental hazards and unauthorized access or damage

metadata.detection_notes: Assess equipment placement considering environmental risks (water, heat, dust), physical access risks, and protection measures (secure mounting, cable locks, environmental controls). Equipment in vulnerable locations or lacking protective measures indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Facility Security Measures
signals.description: Physical security for offices, rooms, and facilities is not designed and implemented.
signals.applicability: Organizations with offices, rooms, and facilities that require physical security measures to protect personnel and assets

metadata.detection_notes: Review facility security measures including locks, alarms, reinforced doors/windows, and security design. Absence of documented security design or implementation of protective measures for offices and facilities indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Storage Media Controls
signals.description: Storage media is not managed through its lifecycle according to classification and handling requirements.
signals.applicability: Organizations using storage media (physical and removable) that requires lifecycle management from acquisition through disposal

metadata.detection_notes: Review media management procedures including inventory, classification, storage, transportation, and disposal. Absence of documented procedures, untracked media, improper storage, or lack of secure disposal processes indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Off-Site Asset Security
signals.description: Off-site assets are not protected considering different risks of working outside organization premises.
signals.applicability: Organizations with assets located outside organizational premises including remote work, mobile computing, and assets at third-party locations

metadata.detection_notes: Review security measures for remote work, mobile devices, portable equipment, and assets at vendor or customer sites. Absence of policies for off-site work, lack of encryption, missing device tracking, or inadequate physical security controls indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Secure Area Working Rules
signals.description: Security measures for working in secure areas are not designed and implemented.
signals.applicability: Organizations with designated secure areas where specific security protocols must be followed during work activities

metadata.detection_notes: Review policies and procedures for working in secure areas including visitor escort requirements, photography restrictions, unattended work rules, and secure area awareness. Absence of documented rules or evidence of enforcement indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Secure Disposal or Re-use Procedures
signals.canonical_name: No Secure Disposal or Re-use Procedures
signals.description: Items containing storage media are not verified to ensure sensitive data is removed before disposal.
signals.applicability: Organizations disposing of or re-using equipment and media that may contain sensitive information

metadata.detection_notes: Review disposal and re-use procedures for equipment and media including data sanitization, physical destruction, verification processes, and certificates of destruction. Absence of documented procedures, unverified disposal, or lack of sanitization indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Physical Security Monitoring
signals.description: Premises are not continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access.
signals.applicability: Organizations requiring continuous monitoring of physical premises to detect and respond to unauthorized access attempts

metadata.detection_notes: Assess whether continuous monitoring systems (CCTV, motion sensors, alarm systems, security personnel) are deployed and actively monitored. Absence of surveillance systems, unmonitored cameras, or lack of 24/7 monitoring indicates this deficiency. Note: A.7.4 is new in ISO 27001:2022.

signals.name: No Physical Security Perimeters
signals.description: Security perimeters are not defined and used to protect areas containing information and assets.
signals.applicability: Organizations with physical facilities that contain sensitive information or information processing equipment

metadata.detection_notes: Review facility documentation for defined security perimeters, physical barriers (walls, fences, gates), and documented access control zones. Absence of clearly defined perimeter boundaries or physical barriers indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Physical and Environmental Threat Protection
signals.canonical_name: No Physical and Environmental Threat Protection
signals.description: Protection against physical and environmental threats is not designed and implemented.
signals.applicability: Organizations requiring protection of information processing facilities from natural disasters, environmental hazards, and deliberate attacks

metadata.detection_notes: Review protection measures against natural disasters (fire, flood, earthquake), environmental threats (temperature, humidity), and malicious attacks. Absence of fire suppression, climate control, flood protection, or structural hardening indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Supporting Utilities Protection
signals.description: Information processing facilities are not protected from power failures and utility disruptions.
signals.applicability: Organizations with information processing facilities dependent on supporting utilities such as power, telecommunications, water, and HVAC systems

metadata.detection_notes: Assess protection measures for critical utilities including UPS systems, backup generators, redundant telecommunications, and HVAC systems. Absence of redundancy, backup power, or utility monitoring indicates this deficiency.

signals.name: No Information Access Restriction
signals.description: Access to information and application system functions is not restricted according to access control policy.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not enforce access restrictions to information and application functions based on defined access control policies, including lack of role-based access control (RBAC), attribute-based access control (ABAC), or need-to-know principles.

metadata.detection_notes: Review access control policies, implemented access controls in applications and systems, permission matrices, role definitions, access provisioning workflows, and enforcement mechanisms for least privilege and need-to-know.

signals.name: Missing Application Security Requirements
signals.description: Information security requirements are not identified, specified, and approved for application development. This signal indicates that applications are developed without documented security requirements, security acceptance criteria, or security specifications for authentication, authorization, data protection, and secure functionality.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all application development projects including web applications, mobile applications, desktop applications, APIs, microservices, cloud applications, and third-party application integrations. Includes both new development and modification of existing applications.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of requirements documentation, functional specifications, security requirements catalogs, acceptance criteria, user stories, and project approval processes. May also be identified through analysis of application development backlogs and security feature tracking.

signals.name: Unprotected Information Systems During Audit Testing
signals.canonical_name: Unprotected Information Systems During Audit Testing
signals.description: Audit tests and activities involving assessment of operational systems are not planned and controlled. This signal indicates that security audits, penetration testing, vulnerability assessments, or compliance testing activities are performed without proper planning, authorization, scope definition, or safeguards to prevent service disruption or data loss.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all audit and assessment activities including internal audits, external audits, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, compliance assessments, security reviews, and system testing that involves operational production systems or sensitive data.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of audit planning procedures, rules of engagement documentation, testing authorization processes, scope definitions, safeguard implementations, and incident records related to audit activities. May also be identified through absence of audit activity controls or planning documentation.

signals.name: No Information Backup
signals.description: Backup copies of information, software, and systems are not maintained and tested regularly.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement regular backups of critical data, systems, and software, or fail to test backup restoration procedures to ensure recoverability in the event of data loss, system failure, or disaster.

metadata.detection_notes: Review backup policies and schedules, backup coverage, backup storage locations (onsite/offsite/cloud), encryption of backups, retention periods, restoration testing procedures, recovery time objectives (RTO), and recovery point objectives (RPO).

signals.name: No Capacity Management
signals.description: Use of resources is not monitored and adjusted with projections for future capacity requirements.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not monitor resource utilization (CPU, memory, storage, network bandwidth) or plan for future capacity needs, risking performance degradation or system unavailability.

metadata.detection_notes: Review capacity monitoring tools, resource utilization metrics, capacity planning processes, growth projections, performance baselines, and alerting mechanisms for capacity thresholds.

signals.name: Missing Change Management
signals.description: Changes to information processing facilities and systems are not subject to change management procedures. This signal indicates that system modifications, configuration changes, software updates, or infrastructure changes are performed without formal approval, testing, documentation, or rollback procedures.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all changes affecting information systems including application code changes, infrastructure modifications, configuration updates, security patches, network changes, database schema modifications, and access control changes. Covers both planned changes and emergency changes.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of change management policies, change approval workflows, change logs and records, deployment procedures, rollback capabilities, and incident analysis. May also be identified through absence of change control boards, approval gates, or change tracking systems.

signals.name: No Clock Synchronization
signals.description: Clocks of information processing systems are not synchronized to approved time sources.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not synchronize system clocks across infrastructure components to approved and accurate time sources (NTP servers, atomic clocks), impacting log correlation, forensic investigations, and compliance.

metadata.detection_notes: Review NTP (Network Time Protocol) configurations, time source accuracy and reliability, clock synchronization monitoring, time drift detection, and timestamp accuracy in logs and audit trails.

signals.name: No Configuration Management
signals.description: Configurations including security configurations are not established, documented, and managed.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not maintain documented baseline configurations for systems, applications, and network devices, or lack processes to manage, track, and enforce configuration standards including security hardening.

metadata.detection_notes: Review configuration management databases (CMDB), baseline configurations, security hardening guides, configuration drift detection, change tracking, and automated configuration enforcement tools (Infrastructure as Code, configuration management tools).

signals.name: Missing Cryptography Controls
signals.description: Rules for effective use of cryptography including key management are not defined and implemented. This signal indicates that cryptographic controls, encryption standards, key management procedures, or cryptographic protocols are not properly established, documented, or enforced across the organization.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems using cryptography including data at rest encryption, data in transit encryption, key management systems, certificate authorities, encryption key storage, cryptographic protocols, digital signatures, and cryptographic libraries. Includes cloud encryption, database encryption, file system encryption, and application-level cryptography.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of cryptography policies, encryption configurations, key management procedures, certificate management systems, protocol configurations, cipher suite selections, and compliance with cryptographic standards. May also be identified through code review, configuration assessments, and cryptographic inventory.

signals.name: No Data Masking
signals.description: Data masking is not used according to access control policy and business requirements.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement data masking, redaction, or obfuscation techniques to protect sensitive information in non-production environments, displays, reports, or for users without need-to-know access.

metadata.detection_notes: Review data masking implementations in test/development environments, production databases, application displays, reporting systems, and compliance with privacy requirements for handling PII, PHI, or payment card data.

signals.name: No Data Leakage Prevention
signals.description: Data leakage prevention measures are not applied to systems and networks handling sensitive information.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement data loss prevention (DLP) technologies and processes to detect and prevent unauthorized disclosure, transfer, or exfiltration of sensitive information through network, endpoint, or cloud channels.

metadata.detection_notes: Review DLP solution deployment (network, endpoint, cloud), DLP policies and rules, monitoring of data transfers, email and web gateway controls, USB/removable media restrictions, and incident response for data leakage events.

signals.name: No Endpoint Security Protection
signals.description: Information stored on, processed by, or accessible via user endpoint devices is not protected.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that allow users to access, process, or store information on endpoint devices (laptops, desktops, mobile devices, tablets) without adequate security controls.

metadata.detection_notes: Review endpoint device policies, endpoint detection and response (EDR) implementations, device management solutions (MDM/UEM), encryption status, and security configurations on user devices.

signals.name: Missing Environment Separation
signals.description: Development, testing, and production environments are not separated and secured. This signal indicates that different environment types share infrastructure, credentials, data, or network access without appropriate isolation controls, potentially allowing development activities to impact production systems or production data to be exposed in non-production environments.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all computing environments including physical servers, virtual machines, cloud environments, containers, databases, network segments, and applications. Covers separation of development, testing, staging, QA, UAT, and production environments across infrastructure, platform, and software layers.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through environment inventory review, network architecture analysis, access control assessments, credential management evaluation, data flow analysis, and deployment pipeline configuration review. May also be identified through examination of environment naming, tagging, and isolation mechanisms.

signals.name: No Information Deletion
signals.description: Information stored in systems and devices is not deleted when no longer required.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not systematically delete or dispose of information that is no longer needed for business or legal purposes, including data on active systems, backups, archived storage, and decommissioned devices.

metadata.detection_notes: Review data retention policies, deletion procedures, secure disposal processes, backup retention schedules, decommissioning procedures for hardware, and compliance with data retention regulations (GDPR right to erasure, etc.).

signals.name: No Logging
signals.description: Logs recording activities, exceptions, faults, and security events are not produced and retained.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement comprehensive logging of user activities, administrative actions, system events, security events, exceptions, and faults, or fail to retain logs for appropriate periods to support incident detection, investigation, and compliance.

metadata.detection_notes: Review logging configurations, log collection and aggregation, log retention policies, protection of log integrity, logging coverage (applications, systems, network devices, security tools), and compliance with regulatory logging requirements.

signals.name: No Malware Protection
signals.description: Protection against malware is not implemented and supported by user awareness.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement anti-malware technologies (antivirus, anti-spyware, EDR) or fail to maintain user awareness about malware threats and safe computing practices.

metadata.detection_notes: Review anti-malware software deployment, signature update status, EDR implementation, email filtering, web filtering, user security awareness training, and malware incident history.

signals.name: No Monitoring Activities
signals.description: Networks, systems, and applications are not monitored for anomalous behavior and appropriate actions taken.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not actively monitor networks, systems, and applications for anomalous behavior, security events, performance issues, or unauthorized activities, and lack processes to respond appropriately to detected anomalies.

metadata.detection_notes: Review security monitoring tools (SIEM, IDS/IPS, EDR), network monitoring, application performance monitoring, anomaly detection capabilities, alert configurations, incident response procedures, and 24/7 monitoring coverage.

signals.name: Inadequate Networks Security
signals.description: Networks and network devices are not secured, managed, and controlled to protect information. This signal indicates that network infrastructure lacks appropriate security controls such as firewalls, intrusion detection/prevention, network access controls, secure configurations, or monitoring capabilities.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all network infrastructure including physical networks, virtual networks, software-defined networks, cloud networking, wireless networks, and network devices such as routers, switches, firewalls, load balancers, and network security appliances.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through network architecture review, firewall rule analysis, network device configuration audits, security group assessments, network monitoring system evaluations, and penetration testing results. May also be identified through network traffic analysis and security posture assessments.

signals.name: Lack of Network Segregation
signals.description: Groups of information services, users, and systems are not segregated in networks. This signal indicates that network segmentation is not implemented to separate different security zones, business functions, or trust levels, potentially allowing unrestricted lateral movement and access.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all network environments including physical networks, virtual networks, cloud networks, data center networks, and wireless networks. Includes separation of production/development/test environments, user/server networks, trusted/untrusted zones, and different business units or security classifications.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through network architecture review, VLAN configuration analysis, firewall rule assessment, subnet design evaluation, cloud network configuration review, and micro-segmentation policy inspection. May also be identified through network mapping and traffic flow analysis.

signals.name: Insecure Network Services
signals.description: Security mechanisms, service levels, and requirements of network services are not identified and implemented. This signal indicates that network services lack documented security requirements, service level agreements, authentication mechanisms, encryption, or appropriate security controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all network services including managed services, cloud services, internet services, internal network services, APIs, third-party network services, and service provider connections. Includes DNS, DHCP, NTP, authentication services, file sharing, messaging, and application services.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of service agreements, network service configurations, security requirements documentation, authentication mechanisms, encryption settings, and service monitoring capabilities. May also be identified through assessment of vendor management processes and service level agreements.

signals.name: Uncontrolled Outsourced Development
signals.description: Organization does not direct, monitor, and review outsourced system development activities. This signal indicates that third-party, contractor, or vendor-led development work lacks appropriate oversight, security requirements, code review, testing verification, or contractual security obligations.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all outsourced development activities including offshore development, contractor engagements, managed service providers, software development agencies, open-source contributions, and any external development resources. Covers custom software development, system integration, and code modifications performed by external parties.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of vendor contracts, service agreements, development oversight procedures, code review processes, security requirements documentation, acceptance testing procedures, and vendor management policies. May also be identified through absence of security clauses in development contracts or lack of code validation processes.

signals.name: No Privileged Access Management
signals.description: Allocation and use of privileged access rights is not restricted and managed.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that grant privileged access rights (administrative, root, superuser) without proper restriction, approval, monitoring, or periodic review mechanisms.

metadata.detection_notes: Review privileged account inventories, approval processes, privileged access management (PAM) solutions, session monitoring, periodic access reviews, and segregation of duties for administrative rights.

signals.name: No Redundancy of Information Processing Facilities
signals.canonical_name: No Redundancy of Information Processing Facilities
signals.description: Information processing facilities are not implemented with redundancy to meet availability requirements.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement redundant infrastructure components (servers, storage, network, power, cooling) necessary to meet defined availability and business continuity requirements for critical systems and services.

metadata.detection_notes: Review infrastructure architecture, high availability configurations, failover mechanisms, load balancing, geographic redundancy, single points of failure, availability SLAs, and disaster recovery capabilities.

signals.name: Missing Secure Development Life Cycle
signals.description: Rules for secure development of software and systems are not established and applied. This signal indicates that the organization lacks a formal secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) with security integrated into planning, design, development, testing, and deployment phases.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all software development activities including custom application development, system integration, infrastructure as code, automation scripts, APIs, microservices, mobile applications, and any software or system modification. Includes internal development teams and third-party development.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of software development policies and procedures, SDLC documentation, security requirements in development projects, security design reviews, threat modeling practices, secure coding standards, and development workflow analysis. May also be identified through absence of security gates in CI/CD pipelines.

signals.name: Missing Secure System Architecture and Engineering Principles
signals.canonical_name: Missing Secure System Architecture and Engineering Principles
signals.description: Principles for engineering secure systems are not established, documented, and applied. This signal indicates that the organization lacks documented security architecture principles, secure design patterns, defense-in-depth strategies, or architectural security controls that should guide system design and engineering decisions.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all system architecture and engineering activities including application architecture, infrastructure architecture, network architecture, cloud architecture, security architecture, data architecture, and integration architecture. Includes both new system design and modification of existing systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of architecture documentation, security design principles, architectural review processes, security architecture frameworks, design review records, and architectural decision logs. May also be identified through absence of security architecture governance and architectural standards.

signals.name: No Secure Authentication
signals.description: Secure authentication technologies and procedures are not implemented based on access restrictions.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not implement secure authentication mechanisms appropriate to the sensitivity of information and systems, including lack of multi-factor authentication (MFA), weak password policies, or insecure authentication protocols.

metadata.detection_notes: Review authentication mechanisms, password policies, multi-factor authentication (MFA) implementation, authentication protocols (SAML, OAuth, OpenID Connect), password strength requirements, account lockout policies, and authentication logging.

signals.name: Missing Secure Coding Practices
signals.description: Secure coding principles are not applied to software development. This signal indicates that developers lack secure coding standards, guidelines, training, or enforcement mechanisms to prevent common vulnerabilities such as injection flaws, authentication bypasses, and insecure data handling.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all software development activities including application code, infrastructure as code, scripts, automation, configuration files, and any software artifacts. Covers all programming languages, frameworks, and development environments including web, mobile, cloud, and embedded systems development.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through code review, static analysis security testing (SAST), secure coding standards documentation review, developer training records, code quality metrics, and vulnerability assessments. May also be identified through presence of common vulnerability patterns in code.

signals.name: Missing Security Testing in Development
signals.description: Security testing processes are not defined and implemented in the development lifecycle. This signal indicates that applications and systems are developed and deployed without appropriate security testing such as static analysis, dynamic analysis, penetration testing, or vulnerability scanning.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all software development and system deployment activities including application development, infrastructure deployment, configuration changes, and system updates. Covers security testing in development, testing, staging, and pre-production environments.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of testing procedures, CI/CD pipeline configurations, security testing tool deployment, test reports and results, acceptance criteria, and development workflow documentation. May also be identified through absence of security testing tools or security test cases.

signals.name: Uncontrolled Software Installation on Operational Systems
signals.canonical_name: Uncontrolled Software Installation on Operational Systems
signals.description: Procedures and measures are not implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems. This signal indicates that software can be installed on production systems without appropriate authorization, validation, testing, or security review processes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any operational system including production servers, workstations, cloud instances, containers, virtual machines, network devices, and embedded systems. Includes operating system packages, application software, libraries, dependencies, scripts, and firmware updates.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through analysis of software deployment policies, change management procedures, application control configurations, package manager policies, container image approval workflows, and endpoint management systems. May also be identified through review of privilege restrictions and installation audit logs.

signals.name: No Source Code Access Control
signals.description: Read and write access to source code, development tools, and libraries is not appropriately managed.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that develop software and do not properly control access to source code repositories, development tools, software libraries, and build environments through appropriate access controls and segregation.

metadata.detection_notes: Review source code repository access controls, version control system permissions, development tool access, library management, branch protection rules, code review requirements, and segregation between development and production environments.

signals.name: Inadequate Test Information Controls
signals.description: Test information is not appropriately selected, protected, and managed. This signal indicates that test data, including production data used in testing, is not properly sanitized, masked, anonymized, or protected, potentially exposing sensitive or personal information in non-production environments.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all testing activities using data including development testing, QA testing, UAT, performance testing, security testing, and training environments. Covers test databases, test files, test datasets, synthetic data generation, and production data copies used for testing purposes.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of test data policies, data masking procedures, test data provisioning processes, access controls on test environments, and analysis of data flows from production to test systems. May also be identified through privacy impact assessments and data classification reviews.

signals.name: Uncontrolled Use of Privileged Utility Programs
signals.canonical_name: Uncontrolled Use of Privileged Utility Programs
signals.description: Use of utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls is not restricted and controlled. This signal indicates that privileged utilities such as system debuggers, disk editors, registry editors, diagnostic tools, and low-level system utilities are available without appropriate access restrictions, logging, or monitoring.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any system or environment where privileged utility programs exist, including operating systems, database management systems, virtualization platforms, container environments, cloud infrastructure, and network devices. Includes both built-in system utilities and third-party diagnostic tools.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through analysis of file system permissions, role-based access control configurations, privileged access management (PAM) policies, system audit logs, and application control policies. May also be identified through review of group memberships, sudo/sudoers configurations, and tool inventory.

signals.name: No Vulnerability Management
signals.description: Information about technical vulnerabilities is not obtained, exposure evaluated, and measures taken.
signals.applicability: Applies to organizations that do not actively identify, assess, prioritize, and remediate technical vulnerabilities in systems, applications, and network infrastructure through vulnerability scanning and patch management processes.

metadata.detection_notes: Review vulnerability scanning tools and schedules, patch management processes, vulnerability assessment reports, remediation timelines, security bulletin subscriptions, and tracking of known vulnerabilities (CVEs).

signals.name: Missing Web Filtering Controls
signals.description: Access to external websites is not managed to reduce exposure to malicious content. This signal indicates that web filtering, URL categorization, content inspection, or safe browsing controls are not implemented to protect against web-based threats such as malware, phishing, and inappropriate content.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems with internet access including workstations, servers, mobile devices, cloud services, and network infrastructure. Includes web browsers, HTTP/HTTPS traffic, proxy servers, secure web gateways, and DNS-based filtering solutions.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through review of proxy server configurations, secure web gateway policies, DNS filtering settings, browser security policies, endpoint protection configurations, and network traffic inspection capabilities. May also be identified through absence of web content filtering solutions or policies.
